summary: Wave-2 pass over the US gaps. False Claims Act: DOJ's annual results releases for FY1998 (cumulative qui tam figures), FY2000, FY2001, FY2003 and FY2005-FY2009 were recovered from the Wayback Machine and stored, adding press-release vintages of total, qui tam and relator-award figures back to FY2000 plus ten FY2008 relator-share cases; FY1999, FY2002 and FY2004 releases were not found. State false claims acts: official series found for Texas (Civil Medicaid Fraud Division recoveries FY2015-FY2025 from the joint interagency reports) and New York (MFCU recoveries under the NY FCA 2018-2020, AG letters released under FOIL), a cumulative California figure and Illinois only as an event; no state publishes relator awards. The GSK 2012 relator share is still not in any court or DOJ record found: the settlement agreements explicitly reserve it. IRS: TIGTA 2009 and 2016 reports read and stored (pre-2006 informant totals, 2009 claim status, submissions and awards FY2011-Feb 2016); GAO-16-20 gives the first yearly count of denied claims (FY2013-Aug 2015) and GAO-11-683 claim status by year; no TIGTA whistleblower reports exist for 2018 and none were found for 2019-2020 or 2012. Also: Supreme Court opinions in Digital Realty (2018) and Polansky (2023) and the AML Whistleblower Improvement Act text (Pub. L. 117-328) stored as events; NHTSA, FinCEN and DOJ pilot pages checked with no new awards or statistics as of early October 2026.

cases.summary: Medicaid best-price rebate underpayments and kickbacks (Zocor, Vioxx); first of two qui tam suits in Merck's $361.5 million settlement. A former Merck employee was the relator.
cases.location: Fact sheet: significant recoveries in fiscal year 2008, Merck item
cases.quote: The United States paid the relator $46.6 million as his share of the settlement under the False Claims Act’s qui tam provisions. In addition to the federal recovery, Merck paid $162 million to state Medicaid programs.
cases.notes: Sanctions = the $221.9 million federal part of this suit. Settled in FY2008 (Oct 2007-Sep 2008) according to DOJ's FY2008 fact sheet; exact date in the original release linked there.

cases.summary: Discounts to hospitals for Pepcid not reported as Medicaid best price; second qui tam suit (a physician relator) in Merck's $361.5 million settlement.
cases.location: Fact sheet: significant recoveries in fiscal year 2008, Merck item

events.title: Supreme Court: Dodd-Frank retaliation protection requires reporting to the SEC (Digital Realty v. Somers)
events.description: The Court held that an employee who reported suspected securities violations only internally, not to the SEC, is not a 'whistleblower' protected by Dodd-Frank's anti-retaliation provision (Sarbanes-Oxley protection remains). Opinion by Justice Ginsburg.
events.quote: Held: Dodd-Frank’s anti-retaliation provision does not extend to an individual, like Somers, who has not reported a violation of the securities laws to the SEC.

events.title: Supreme Court: government may dismiss qui tam suits it joins at any stage (Polansky)
events.description: 8-1 decision (Kagan, J.): the government may move to dismiss a qui tam suit whenever it has intervened, during the seal period or later; courts apply the ordinary Rule 41(a) standard. Justice Thomas, dissenting, and Justice Kavanaugh (with Barrett), concurring, said there are substantial arguments that qui tam is inconsistent with Article II and that the Court should consider the issue in an appropriate case.
events.quote: The Government may move to dismiss an FCA action under §3730(c)(2)(A) whenever it has intervened—whether during the seal period or later on.

programs.name: New York False Claims Act qui tam (State Finance Law §§187-194)
programs.notes: New York State's own false claims act, enforced by the Attorney General (Medicaid cases by its Medicaid Fraud Control Unit). Whistleblowers (qui tam plaintiffs) get 15-25 percent of the state's recovery if the state or a local government takes over the case, 25-30 percent if they pursue it alone, and at most 10 percent when the case rests mainly on public information. HHS-OIG has approved the law for the section 1909 Medicaid incentive, so New York keeps an extra 10 percentage points of Medicaid recoveries. Since 2019 the AG must report MFCU recoveries under the act to the Legislature every April; only the 2018-2020 letters were found (released under FOIL). Enactment date not confirmed from an official text read here.

programs.name: California False Claims Act qui tam (Government Code §12650 et seq.)
programs.notes: California's false claims act, enforced by the Attorney General's False Claims Unit (Corporate Fraud Section) and the Division of Medi-Cal Fraud and Elder Abuse, or by local prosecutors. Whistleblowers can file qui tam suits under seal and share in recoveries. HHS-OIG-approved for the section 1909 incentive. The AG publishes no annual series of recoveries or relator awards; only a ten-year cumulative figure (2026 press release) was found. Enactment date and award percentages not read from an official text here.

programs.name: Texas Medicaid Fraud Prevention Act qui tam (Human Resources Code ch. 36)
programs.notes: Texas's Medicaid-only false claims law, enforced by the Attorney General's Civil Medicaid Fraud Division (renamed Healthcare Program Enforcement Division in FY2024). Private persons can file qui tam suits and share in recoveries. Yearly division totals (all cases, not only qui tam) are published in the Joint Annual Interagency Coordination Report of the Texas HHS Inspector General and the AG (Texas Government Code 531.103), Texas fiscal year September-August. HHS-OIG-approved for the section 1909 incentive. Relator awards are not reported separately; award percentages not read from the statute here (texas.gov statute site did not answer scripts).

programs.name: Illinois False Claims Act qui tam (740 ILCS 175)
programs.notes: Illinois's false claims act (formerly the Whistleblower Reward and Protection Act, per secondary sources), enforced by the Attorney General; amended in July 2010 (HB 5951). HHS-OIG-approved for the section 1909 incentive. No official series of recoveries or relator awards was found.
